solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S023-01.notes: Few unneeded words, short paragraphs = spare; ornate/digressive/effusive are opposites. 'Spare' as an adjective is slightly less familiar, but the clue is strong.

S023-02.notes: Bright bands that are easy to notice = conspicuous; drab/subtle contradict it, variable is off-point.

S023-03.notes: 'however' interrupts subject and verb ('colonies ... showed'), so it takes a pair of commas; the opening comma is already in the passage. A has no closing comma; C and D put a semicolon between subject and verb.

S023-04.notes: 'By the time it arrives' (in 2031) is a future reference point, so it needs the future perfect. Past perfect and present perfect are traps.

S023-05.notes: The final choice after extensive testing = Ultimately. Instead implies a rejected alternative that the passage does not set up; For example and Similarly don't fit.

S023-06.notes: Only C includes the rarity of nearly complete skeletons.

S023-07.notes: When moisture is everywhere, the lichen grows on every side, so the north-side pattern comes from dampness, not from which way the surface faces. A overstates the evidence; B and C aren't supported.

S023-08.notes: Only B covers both parts of the claim: faster in every genre, and the smallest gap for poetry (3, 4, 0.5). C and D cover only part of it.

S023-09.notes: He still wakes at 4:29 and watches the bus leave, so his old routine continues. B overreaches; C and D contradict the text (he is retired, and he no longer sets the alarm).

S023-10.notes: A possessive relative pronoun is needed before 'performance'. 'who's' (= who is) is the main trap; 'her' creates a comma splice.
